Speedtest can tell you whether your internet is actually slow, JustDelete.me helps you find the account deletion pages companies bury in their settings, and AlternativeTo can point you toward free software that does the same job as something you’re paying for. These are the kinds of websites that solve annoying problems in a few clicks, without making you download another app or sign up for a subscription.

Some are especially useful for everyday tasks. TinyPNG makes image files smaller without noticeably hurting their quality, PhotoRoom can turn an ordinary product photo into something that looks professionally shot, and Excalidraw lets you sketch ideas and collaborate without learning complicated design software. Then there are tools like ManualsLib, which can save you from digging through drawers or contacting customer support just to figure out how an old appliance works.

A lot of useful corners of the internet are surprisingly easy to miss. Search engines tend to push the biggest platforms, while smaller tools that do one thing really well get overlooked. You probably won’t need all ten of these websites every day, but having them bookmarked can save you time, money, and a lot of unnecessary frustration when you do.
